SinghMunch (Sher-e-Punjab) — Full Stack Ordering PlatformLiveIndia ClientSolo build
›

Client had no digital storefront — orders, menu updates, and payments were all handled manually by phone with no online system.

Full-stack ordering platform for a pure-vegetarian Punjabi restaurant: Next.js 14 storefront + NestJS API across two separate repos, with Razorpay payments, PDF receipts, and an admin dashboard for menu and order management — shipped as an installable PWA and packaged as an Android TWA app.

26REST endpoints
2repos, one API contract
PWA + Androidinstallable app
Server-side price and stock recomputation on every order — the client can never influence the charged amount. Razorpay payments (cash-on-delivery and online) confirmed through two independent paths — client-side checkout verification and a signed webhook — both HMAC-SHA256 verified with constant-time comparison, and made idempotent via a conditional atomic update so stock only decrements and the receipt email only sends once, regardless of which path fires first (or both). On-demand PDF receipts rendered with PDFKit and emailed via Resend. Google Sign-In verified server-side against Google's own token endpoint — the API never trusts a client-asserted identity. Shipped as a PWA with an offline service worker and distributed separately as an Android Trusted Web Activity app. Deployed as a Vercel serverless function with a cached NestJS bootstrap for warm-start reuse, with a Railway/Nixpacks config as a fallback deployment target from the same codebase.

Writing
AI for Developers series
7-part series on how modern AI systems actually work — written for engineers, not researchers
7
Agent Memory — how AI systems remember across sessions
Short-term vs long-term memory, why context windows aren't enough, and how production agents carry state forward.
6
Multi-Agent Systems — splitting work across specialists
Why one agent doing everything has a ceiling, and how orchestrators coordinate specialists to solve bigger problems.
5
MCP — the universal plug for AI agents
How Model Context Protocol lets any agent connect to any tool without custom glue code.
4
AI Agents — when an LLM can act, not just answer
Tool use, dynamic chaining, and why agents replace if/else logic with reasoning-driven execution.
3
RAG — answering questions from your own data
How retrieval-augmented generation lets an LLM work with documents it was never trained on.
2
Embeddings — coordinates for meaning
How text becomes numbers, why similar meanings cluster together, and why this powers AI search.
1
LLMs — what they actually are and aren't
The mental model every developer needs before building on top of AI systems.
